evidence.quote: A 35-year-old male was brought to the emergency department for mutism, immobility, and refusal to eat.

We present a 35-year-old male with longstanding developmental delays who was repeatedly diagnosed with psychosis and treated with antipsychotics. He developed catatonia during his course of treatment.
A 35-year-old male was brought to the emergency department for mutism, immobility, and refusal to eat.
A 35-year-old male was brought to the emergency department for mutism, immobility, and refusal to eat.

claims.text: He was brought to the emergency department with mutism, immobility and refusal to eat; on admission he was mute and immobile with negativism and posturing consistent with catatonia. He lacked the ability to communicate, was unresponsive and poorly groomed, and the physical examination was otherwise unremarkable. Neuroimaging, liver and renal function, blood tests and EEG were reported normal. The authors attribute the catatonia to protracted antipsychotic exposure.
